text:
maria: Heads up — customer asked to manage burst windows from their VPC control plane. They want per-org baseline + per-key bursts that can be tuned independently. Thoughts?

aj: we already have per-org and per-key limits in hosted. main question is enforcement point for Private: agent-level (local), gateway (central inside VPC), or both?

cheng: local enforcement is lowest latency and avoids extra hops, but then telemetry aggregation becomes trickier. Also harder to do cross-key global caps.

samir: agree. For Private deployments customers want to be able to upload their own JSON/YAML policy and have it enforced locally without calling our control plane. We can support a "managed policy" mode where they push via S3/KMS and the agent watches it.

maria: UX ask from console: allow upload + preview diff of effective rules (inheritance: org -> app -> key). Need clear warnings for dangerous configs (eg. infinite burst).

aj: proposal: default enforcement is local with an optional central sync for observability. Local enforcement reads policies from `/etc/redwood/rate_policies/` and exposes enforcement metrics to the telemetry exporter if allowed.

cheng: what about burst semantics? token-bucket with two levels: short-term burst (60s window), sustained burst (1h smoothing). Customer wants to set both and a global safety cap.

samir: example policy snippet customers could upload (YAML):
```
policies:
  org: org_foo
  default:
    per_minute: 6000
    burst:
      short_window_sec: 60
      short_burst_tokens: 1200
      long_window_sec: 3600
      long_burst_tokens: 18000
  api_keys:
    key_abc123:
      per_minute: 1200
      burst:
        short_burst_tokens: 400
```

maria: love the explicitness. We should also include an automatic "safety_reduction" knob applied by runtime if overall GPU queue depth is high. So local agent can degrade bursts gracefully.

aj: question for security: who can upload? RBAC. Private control plane should support signed policies and a rollout window. Maybe we only allow uploads that are signed with enterprise KMS key.

cheng: telemetry: we need per-policy_id counters, token_usage, reject_reasons. Also a sampling of denied requests to tie to debug traces. Customers want to see when their bursts hit safety caps.

quota-bot: policy-deploy event: policy "org_foo/20240321-4" uploaded by samir, staged -> active in 30s (simulated). :rocket: 

samir: implementation notes — agent will: 1) validate policy schema, 2) compute flattened effective limits per key, 3) load into in-process token-bucket layer, 4) expose metrics: `redwood.rate.allowed`, `redwood.rate.throttled`, `redwood.rate.tokens_remaining`.

maria: console UX: when a customer uploads, show three columns: declared policy, effective per-key table, and a simulated QPS curve with projected throttles. Need small help text: "Short burst = instantaneous extra tokens consumed over 60s".

aj: also need backward compatibility for existing Dedicated customers who currently have external ratepolicies via API. Provide a migration path: import -> validate -> dry-run -> activate. Dry-run should surface expected throttles for last 24h traffic.

cheng: edge case: cross-key aggregation (org-wide). If local agent enforces per-key only, org-wide cap could be violated when keys are used on different nodes. To support org caps we need a shared counter (Redis inside VPC) or a periodic sync with approximate counts. Both have tradeoffs.

samir: propose: tiered approach: if org-wide cap present, require a shared counter backend (we support Redis/Postgres) in the VPC. If customer opts out, warn that org caps will be best-effort only.

maria: can we add a console toggle: "Require strong org caps (requires shared backend)" with checklist of infra needed.

aj: security + audit: every local enforcement decision should tag the policy_id used and the policy_git_sha (or S3 etag). Log both to audit stream.

cheng: for rollout UX: allow canary percent by key prefix (eg: keys starting with `canary-`) so they can test burst changes on a subset. Also allow timeboxed rollouts.

maria: OK action items: samir to draft agent schema + validation rules; aj to write migration doc and RBAC requirements; cheng to spec telemetry metrics and Redis-backed org counters; I will mock console screens and copy for help text.

samir: I started a tiny draft here: https://internal.redwood/schemas/vpc-rate-policy-draft.md — will push a sample JSON and unit tests by EOD.

aj: thanks. ping me when draft is in the repo. Also add an example of policy rejection messages so console can show inline hints (eg. `burst_tokens > long_window * per_minute/60` -> "burst too large for sustained rate").

maria: perfect. feel free to @mention product-legal if we need additional compliance notes for customers who control their own enforcement.

cheng: one last note — keep default metrics cardinality low: aggregate by policy_id and region, avoid per-key label explosion unless customer enables key-level observability.

maria: nice. closing loop: we'll present this design in next week's infra sync. Thanks all :thumbsup:
